n1.notes: Refarmed 3G/4G core band; widely deployed for 5G NSA/SA coverage layers in Europe and Asia.

n3.notes: Most common LTE band globally, increasingly refarmed to NR via DSS.

n5.notes: Low-band coverage layer in the Americas and Oceania.

n7.notes: Mid-band capacity layer, common in Europe, LATAM and Canada.

n25.notes: Superset of PCS; used by T-Mobile/Sprint heritage networks in the US.

n28.notes: Primary 5G coverage band in Europe, APAC and LATAM; excellent indoor penetration.

n38.notes: TDD slice inside the 2.6 GHz IMT-E gap; used in Europe.

n40.notes: Capacity band in India, China, and parts of APAC.

n41.notes: T-Mobile US 'Ultra Capacity' workhorse and China Mobile's primary 5G band; up to 100 MHz carriers.

n48.notes: US shared-spectrum (CBRS) band, popular for private 5G networks.

n66.notes: North American mid-band; superset of LTE Band 4.

n71.notes: T-Mobile US 'Extended Range 5G' low-band coverage layer.

n75.notes: Supplemental downlink band used in Europe.

n77.notes: Superset of n78; includes US C-Band (3.7–3.98 GHz) and Japan's 3.3–4.2 GHz allocations.

n78.notes: The most widely deployed 5G mid-band worldwide; the global capacity workhorse.

n79.notes: Used in China, Japan and Russia; often absent from devices sold in the Americas/Europe.

n261.notes: Verizon's original 5G Ultra Wideband band; subset of n257.
